question: A grocer marked his goods 80% above the cost price and sold them at a discount of X%. If he made a profit of 8%, find the value of X.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume CP = 100

MP = 100 + 80% = 180

Profit 8% ⇒ SP = 108

Discount = 180 − 108 = 72 ⇒ % = (72 ÷ 180) × 100

**∴ Answer = 40%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price = 80% more than Cost Price

Profit = 8%

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 + Profit%)

MP = CP × (1 + Markup%)

Discount% = [(MP − SP) ÷ MP] × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP = 100

⇒ MP = 100 + 80% of 100 = 180

⇒ SP = 100 + 8% of 100 = 108

⇒ Discount = 180 − 108 = 72

⇒ Discount% = (72 ÷ 180) × 100

⇒ Discount% = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price Concept

MP = CP × (1 + Markup%)

Profit Formula

SP = CP × (1 + Profit%)

Discount Formula

Discount% = [(MP − SP) ÷ MP] × 100

Shortcut Idea

Always assume CP = 100 to simplify percentage problems
